run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: I could not corroborate the reported incident from the requested log index, and no root cause can be named from the available evidence. The Elasticsearch source contains exactly one index, app-261-prod-logs, holding only 4 documents in total; across the whole authorized window (2026-10-24T17:26:27Z to 2026-11-23T17:26:27Z) it matched 4 documents, all level INFO, all timestamped between 2026-11-23T17:01:19Z and 17:26:19Z, i.e. roughly 5.5 hours after the reported ~11:26Z incident and with cluster=production-eu-west-2. Those four lines report healthy checkout-service status (p95 latency 215ms/220ms, success rate 99.8%) and healthy payment-service provider connections. A query of the same index for the reported incident period (2026-11-23T10:26:00Z to 12:26:00Z) returned nothing, so there are no log lines to explain 500s at that time. Prometheus and Jaeger were both unreachable on every attempt (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, latency and span evidence for the window is unknown rather than zero. In Kubernetes, every otel-demo object was created 2026-11-23T14:36–14:38Z, after the alleged incident; the checkout deployment (generation 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) is Available with one ReplicaSet, its pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf is Running/ready with 0 restarts, and its available log lines (17:21:23Z–17:25:47Z) show successful PlaceOrder → payment → email sequences. The flagd fault-injection ConfigMap has every flag's defaultVariant set to off at query time, which is a post-incident reading and cannot establish what was in effect at 11:26Z. I found no evidence of checkout 500s, no affected entity I can name from its own error signal, and no object that applied a fault.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source contains a single index, app-261-prod-logs (health green, docs.count 4, store.size 6.7kb); no other log index exists there.

Across the full authorized window 2026-10-24T17:26:27Z–2026-11-23T17:26:27Z, index app-261-prod-logs matched exactly 4 documents, all level INFO, split by service into checkout-service (3) and payment-service (1), and all four fell in the single date_histogram bucket 2026-11-23T12:00:00Z–18:00:00Z.

The only four log documents in the index read: checkout-service "Healthy: p95 latency 215ms" at 2026-11-23T17:26:19Z, checkout-service "Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes" at 17:21:19Z, payment-service "All payment provider connections healthy" at 17:11:19Z and checkout-service "Healthy: p95 latency 220ms" at 17:01:19Z, each with cluster=production-eu-west-2.

The only checkout/payment log lines that exist report healthy behaviour (p95 215–220ms, success rate 99.8%, payment provider connections healthy) and were written at 17:01–17:26Z, about 5.5 hours after the reported ~11:26Z incident; they neither record 500s nor describe the incident period.

All otel-demo and kube-system pods visible in the cluster were created 2026-11-23T14:36:07Z–14:38:05Z, every one is phase Running with ready=true and restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason; the checkout pod is checkout-6578865d87-v6flf created 2026-11-23T14:36:30Z, whose ReplicaSet owner is checkout-6578865d87.

The checkout Deployment (namespace otel-demo) was created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z at generation 1 with container image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and conditions Available=True, Progressing=True; the payment Deployment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) and the flagd Deployment (image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8) were created at the same instant, so these workloads postdate the alleged incident.

Checkout container logs of pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf between 2026-11-23T17:21:23Z and 17:25:47Z show repeated successful PlaceOrder sequences followed by "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent", with severity info.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json in which every fault-injection flag is present and ENABLED but with defaultVariant "off", including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad.

If the 500s were a checkout-side fault injected through flagd (the paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable flags in ConfigMap flagd-config), the flags would have had to be non-default during 11:26Z; the only reading available is at ~17:26Z where every defaultVariant is "off", so this candidate is neither confirmed nor excluded.

A failing payment dependency reached from checkout remains an unverified candidate: no payment or checkout error/latency series or spans could be read because the Prometheus and Jaeger sources were unavailable, and the post-incident payment log line reports healthy provider connections only.

gaps: The query of index app-261-prod-logs for the reported incident window 2026-11-23T10:26:00Z–12:26:00Z returned 0 documents (status no_data), so whether checkout-service or payment-service logged anything at ~11:26Z is unknown; the index holds only 4 documents in total across the whole authorized month, none of them in that window.

Prometheus was unreachable on five separate calls (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules) all returning SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error rates, ERROR-status span counts, latency and targets for the incident window are unknown rather than zero.

Jaeger was unreachable on three calls (traces_list_services twice, traces_search once) returning SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace or error-span evidence for checkout or any dependency exists in this Run.

Kubernetes state cannot describe the incident: every object (pods, deployments, replicasets, configmaps) in the accessible cluster was created 2026-11-23T14:36–14:38Z, after the alleged incident, and a grouped query over all namespaces returned no events at all; the incident-time pod, rollout and probe state is unknown.
Change history is not integrated (not_integrated: change_history), so nothing can be said about who changed flagd flags, images or configuration around 11:26Z.
The checkout pod's readable log only reaches back to 2026-11-23T17:21:23Z (285 lines, ~4 minutes), so its behaviour at 11:26Z is entirely unknown.
The exact incident time is taken from the request ("6 hours ago", ~2026-11-23T11:26Z relative to the 17:26:27Z window end) and could not be confirmed by any alert, event or trace evidence.
next_steps: Restore or check the Prometheus and Jaeger read paths (both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and re-query traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"} and rpc_*_duration/count series for 2026-11-23T10:30–12:30Z to measure error rate and latency during the reported window.

Check whether log shipping from the checkout/payment containers to app-261-prod-logs was working at 11:26Z (the index contains only 4 INFO lines for the whole month) and identify the collector or ingest path that should have delivered ERROR/exception lines.
Obtain the exact incident start time and any alert payload from the alerting system to replace the inferred ~11:26Z window.

Verify from a change log (change_history is not integrated here) whether any flagd flag in ConfigMap flagd-config, or any checkout/payment deployment change, was applied around 11:26Z, since the current post-incident reading shows all flags at defaultVariant "off".

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
view.incomplete_reason: limit: the newest 30 of 285 matching lines are shown

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: The tool filtered timestamp to the query window; this filter cannot be turned off.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.
